summary: Parallel read-only spec of the *mut conversion for the remaining check-expr spine + collect routing

apply_order: STEP 0 (prerequisite, do NOT use spec #1's wholesale 9-arm dispatcher block): spec #1 lists 9 leaves but only 5 are actually specified (#2 Ident, #3 Binary, #5 FieldAccess, #4 Call, #6 MethodCall). The other 4 arms (ExprPath/ExprUnary/ExprIndex/ExprStructLit) have NO leaf spec. Pasting spec #1's match breaks the build (its own risk note admits 'will not compile until all 9 exist'). Wire arms INCREMENTALLY, one per defined leaf, each inserted between line 2471 (ExprReturn) and line 2472 (_ => checker_check_expr_mut). Name-collision: use spec #2's name checker_check_ident_expr_inplace, NOT spec #1's checker_check_ident_inplace.

STEP 1 — spec #7 (COLLECT): add 4 Mut* result structs (MutFieldDefsResult/MutFieldDefListResult/MutVariantsResult/MutVariantListResult), checker_collect_field_def_list_mut + checker_collect_field_defs_mut (delegate only to checker_lower_type_expr_mut), checker_collect_variant_list_mut + checker_collect_variants_mut, checker_collect_struct_def_inplace, checker_collect_enum_def_inplace (in-place (*c).structs/enums.entries[id as usize] writes, caps 128/32), AND the leaf checker_collect_item_bridge. Rewrite checker_collect_item_inplace (2267-2274): add ItemStruct/ItemEnum arms, and CRITICALLY move the residual `_ =>` inline (*c).collect_item(item) into checker_collect_item_bridge. The bridge extraction is necessary-and-sufficient for the collect-side frame; the new arms alone do NOT fix it.

STEP 2 — spec #2 (ExprIdent leaf): add checker_check_ident_expr_inplace (no bridge needed; (*c).env.lookup + (*c).borrows store-back + checker_report_error_at_inplace + checker_is_linear_type_inplace). Wire arm `ExprIdent => checker_check_ident_expr_inplace(c, e)`.

STEP 3 — spec #3 (ExprBinary leaf): add checker_check_binary_expr_inplace + its real *mut children checker_check_binary_op_types_inplace, checker_check_binary_units_inplace, checker_report_unit_mismatch_inplace, and its THREE isolated leaf bridges checker_check_hyper_binary_bridge / checker_record_hyper_expr_bridge / checker_eval_const_int_denom_is_zero_bridge. Operands recurse via checker_check_opt_expr_inplace. Wire arm `ExprBinary => checker_check_binary_expr_inplace(c, e)`.

STEP 4 — spec #5 (ExprFieldAccess leaf): add checker_check_field_access_inplace (no bridge; receiver via checker_check_opt_expr_inplace, errors via checker_report_error_at_inplace, all helpers are free fns / (*c) reads). Wire arm `ExprFieldAccess => checker_check_field_access_inplace(c, e)`.

STEP 5 — spec #4 (ExprCall leaf) + spec #6 (ExprMethodCall leaf), landed together because they SHARE bridges (consolidate, do not double-define): one canonical set of arg/effects/borrow leaf bridges wrapping (*c).check_call_args, (*c).check_callee_effects [effect row `with Mut, IO, Panic, Div` — NO Alloc], (*c).release_call_arg_borrows, plus checker_check_expr_list_no_type_no_linear_consume_mut. Add checker_check_call_expr_inplace (clean TyFn path inline; everything else delegated to existing checker_check_expr_mut leaf) and checker_check_method_call_inplace. Wire arms `ExprCall => checker_check_call_expr_inplace(c, e)` and `ExprMethodCall => checker_check_method_call_inplace(c, e)`.

STEP 6 — fixed-point + sweep confirmation: rebuild bin/souc, verify gen2==gen3 self-reproduction, run the wide run-pass + compile-fail sweep before overwriting canonical bin/souc (collect store-back has silently corrupted unrelated returns in repo history).
plan.layer_batches:
4 build+gate layers, batched by inert-vs-live (each layer = one serial build + one --check gate; gate-or-revert):

LAYER 1 = collect (spec #7). ISOLATED because it is the only layer that changes table-WRITE semantics and is bootstrap-fixed-point-sensitive (in-place store-back has silently corrupted unrelated returns in repo history). Also dependency-forced FIRST: --check runs collect before check, and every realistic gate input (specs #5/#6/#7) contains structs/enums, so if the collect-side frame is unfixed those inputs crash at collect before any expr arm runs. Gate: spec #7 gate_input (Point struct + Shape enum + area fn) AND min_empty (ItemFn regression). Reconfirm gen2==gen3 + wide sweep here.

LAYER 2 = leaf-expr (specs #2 Ident, #3 Binary, #5 FieldAccess). BATCHED because they are bridge-light and their only failure mode is a compile error (file:line, no bisection needed) — batching 3 cheap leaves saves 2 serial builds. Land all three leaves + their 3 inline dispatch arms together. Gate: min_let / two_fn with the arithmetic exercised in TAIL position (see global_risks on let-RHS vacuity).

LAYER 3 = call+method (specs #4 Call, #6 MethodCall). ISOLATED from Layer 2 because these are the bridge-HEAVY leaves where frame-isolation and effect-row (the Mut,IO,Panic,Div-no-Alloc callee_effects row) mistakes hide; isolating them means a tight-stack overflow bisects to exactly this layer. Their shared arg/effects/borrow bridges are consolidated into one set. Gate: two_fn (clean TyFn call) then hello (method call on a struct).

LAYER 4 = dispatch / fixed-point confirm (STEP 6). Final hello rung + gen2==gen3 self-reproduction + wide run-pass/compile-fail sweep as a separate bisectable rung before overwriting canonical bin/souc. Maps the schema's collect / leaf-expr / call+method / dispatch with a real inert-vs-live justification, not just naming.
global_risks: GATE STACK SIZE IS NOT 8MB IN ANY SHIPPED SCRIPT. Verified: native_v2_e2e_exit_code_gate.sh and canonical_compiler_gate.sh both set `ulimit -s 1048576` (1 GB); other gates use `unlimited` or 64MB. An 8-12MB frame cannot overflow 1GB, so these scripts AS-WRITTEN cannot validate a frame-size fix — they pass even with the bug present (gate-or-revert would measure nothing). The `--check@8MB` gate must be run MANUALLY as `( ulimit -s 8192; ./bin/souc --check input.sio; echo $? )` and must exit 0. State this in the run command for every layer.

VACUOUS-PASS for let-RHS expressions. Verified by inspection: checker_check_stmt_inplace (2422) routes StmtLet/StmtVar/StmtAssign through the BY-VALUE checker_check_stmt_bridge (2424/2425/2427), so a `let s = a + b` checks its RHS by value and NEVER hits the new arms. Only TAIL exprs and bare expr-statements reach the *mut spine: StmtExpr → checker_check_expr_stmt_inplace (2431) → checker_check_opt_expr_inplace (2435) → checker_check_expr_inplace (2450). So gate inputs must exercise the target expr in TAIL position (e.g. fn body whose last expr is `a + b`, `id(s)`, `c.bump(2)`, `t.foo`), not buried in a `let`. The spec gate_inputs that put work in let-bindings are partially vacuous; their tail-expr line is the real driver.

SPEC #1's WHOLESALE 9-ARM DISPATCHER IS NOT AN APPLY ARTIFACT. Only 5 of the 9 referenced leaves are specified; pasting it references 4 undefined fns (ExprPath/ExprUnary/ExprIndex/ExprStructLit handlers) and breaks the build. Wire arms incrementally per leaf. Leave those 4 kinds on the `_ => checker_check_expr_mut` fallback. Name-collision: spec #1 says checker_check_ident_inplace; the defining spec #2 says checker_check_ident_expr_inplace — use the latter.

BRIDGE DEDUP. Spec #4 defines checker_check_call_args_bridge / _callee_effects_bridge / _release_call_arg_borrows_bridge (return i64); spec #6 defines _mut variants of the SAME THREE by-value methods (return unit). They wrap identical (*c) methods. Consolidate to ONE canonical set in Layer 3 or you ship redundant duplicate leaves (and risk a duplicate-definition compile error).

EFFECT-ROW PRECISION. checker_check_callee_effects_* must be `with Mut, IO, Panic, Div` (NO Alloc) to match by-value check_callee_effects (check.sio:6234); the other arg/borrow bridges carry Alloc. A mismatched effect annotation fails the effect-subset check at the call site.

FRAME-ISOLATION IS THE LOAD-BEARING INVARIANT for Layers 1/3. NO inline (*c).<method returning Checker or (Checker,TypeEntry)> may appear in any hot *mut function — every such call compile-allocates its multi-MB SRET in the enclosing frame regardless of runtime branch. The collect `_ =>` bridge extraction (Layer 1) and the call/method shared leaf bridges (Layer 3) are mandatory, not cosmetic. Do not 'optimize' by inlining a bridge body.

FIXED-POINT / SWEEP before overwriting canonical bin/souc. The collect change (Layer 1) mutates table-write semantics; repo history shows in-place store-back silently corrupting unrelated returns when a guard is too broad. After Layers 1 and 4, reconfirm gen2==gen3 AND run the full wide run-pass + compile-fail sweep, not just the layer gate.

DEPTH DOUBLE-COUNT: converted leaf handlers must NOT re-bracket expr_depth — the dispatcher checker_check_expr_inplace already increments (2455)/decrements (2474-2476). A handler that re-enters check_expr_depth makes every expr count twice and trips spurious MAX_EXPR_DEPTH (error 61) on deep-but-legal programs.
plan.summary: Dependency-sorted, leaves-first, 4 build+gate layers. ORDER: Layer 1 collect (spec #7) — forced first because --check runs collect before check and every realistic gate input has structs/enums, plus it is the only fixed-point-sensitive layer (isolate for bisection). Layer 2 leaf-expr (Ident #2, Binary #3, FieldAccess #5) — batched, bridge-light, compile-error-only failure mode. Layer 3 call+method (#4, #6) — isolated, bridge-heavy, shared arg/effects/borrow bridges consolidated. Layer 4 dispatch + fixed-point/sweep confirm. Every leaf delegates only to already-*mut children: checker_check_opt_expr_inplace (2435), checker_lower_type_expr_mut, checker_report_error_at_inplace (1980), the existing isolated leaf checker_check_expr_mut (1146) as the `_` fallback. Verified by inspection: (1) the fn-body spine block→stmts→stmt→expr-stmt is already *mut (2381/2401/2422/2431), so TAIL-position exprs drive the new arms non-vacuously, but let/var/assign RHS route through the by-value checker_check_stmt_bridge and stay vacuous — gate inputs must use tail position. (2) NO shipped gate runs at 8MB (all are 1GB/unlimited/64MB), so the frame-size win must be checked manually with `ulimit -s 8192` or gate-or-revert measures nothing. (3) Do NOT paste spec #1's 9-arm block (only 5 leaves exist; name-collision on the ident leaf). PASS PROGRESSION: min_empty (after L1, ItemFn+empty main, exits 0) → min_let (after L2, struct/enum collect + tail binary expr `a+b`) → two_fn (after L3, clean-TyFn call `id(s)` in tail) → hello (after L3/L4, method call + field access through full *mut spine, gen2==gen3 reconfirmed).

specs.method: EXTEND the existing *mut dispatcher checker_check_expr_inplace (check.sio:2450). The depth-guard wrapper (2451-2455) and depth-decrement (2474-2476) stay UNCHANGED; only the inner `match e.kind` block (2456-2473) gains 9 new arms. Each new arm routes a common non-literal ExprKind to a dedicated *mut leaf handler (checker_check_<kind>_inplace), inserted between the existing `ExprReturn` arm (2471) and the `_ => checker_check_expr_mut(c, e)` catch-all (2472). Literal/return arms (IntLit, FloatLit, BoolTrue, BoolFalse, StringLit, CharLit, Return) are already inline and stay as-is. checker_check_expr_mut REMAINS the final `_` fallback for the ~17 still-unconverted kinds (If/Match/While/Loop/Block/Break/Continue/ArrayLit/TupleLit/Range/Cast/Handle/Closure/Contest/AuditAttach/ForIn/Error). new_functions = the rewritten dispatcher ONLY; the 9 leaf handlers are listed in deps_needing_conversion (the dispatcher will not compile until all 9 exist). Frame-isolation is preserved because every new arm is a tail-call to a *mut leaf — no by-value Checker-returning call (no (*c).method(...)) appears inline in the dispatcher; the single by-value bridge stays quarantined inside checker_check_expr_mut (1146).
deps: checker_check_ident_inplace(c: *mut Checker, e: Expr) -> TypeEntry — FRESH TRANSCRIPTION, not a method conversion: ExprIdent has NO named by-value method; its logic is inline in check_expr at 12451-12468 (let ident_ty = (*c).env.lookup(e.name); if checker_is_linear_type_inplace(c, ident_ty) [reuse, 2067] && (*c).suppress_linear_consume_depth == 0 { if (*c).borrows.is_borrowed(e.name) { checker_report_error_at_inplace(c, e.span, 38, 0,0,0) [reuse, 1980] } else { let cr = (*c).borrows.consume_linear(e.name); (*c).borrows = cr.0; if cr.1 != 0 { checker_report_error_at_inplace(c, e.span, cr.1, 0,0,0) } } }; return ident_ty). MUST rewrite the by-value `c2 = c2.report_error_at(...)` SRET pattern as the *mut checker_report_error_at_inplace, and mutate (*c).borrows in place.

checker_check_path_expr_inplace(c: *mut Checker, e: Expr) -> TypeEntry — convert check_path_expr (12503). Pure lookups (enums.find / find_variant_enum / env.lookup) returning ty_named/lookup; no by-value Checker mutation, so a straight (*c).field rewrite suffices.

checker_check_binary_expr_inplace(c: *mut Checker, e: Expr) -> TypeEntry — convert check_binary_expr (12527). Recurse via checker_check_opt_expr_inplace(c, e.left/e.right) [reuse, 2435]; the report_error_at calls (e.g. effect-36, and check_binary_op_types which itself returns Checker) must go through checker_report_error_at_inplace / a dedicated check_binary_op_types bridge leaf — NOT inline by-value.
checker_check_unary_expr_inplace(c: *mut Checker, e: Expr) -> TypeEntry — convert check_unary_expr (12471 target).
checker_check_field_access_inplace(c: *mut Checker, e: Expr) -> TypeEntry — convert check_field_access (12472 target).
checker_check_index_expr_inplace(c: *mut Checker, e: Expr) -> TypeEntry — convert check_index_expr (12473 target).

checker_check_method_call_inplace(c: *mut Checker, e: Expr) -> TypeEntry — convert check_method_call (12474 target); arg-list traversal must use checker_check_opt_expr_inplace, not the by-value walker.
checker_check_call_expr_inplace(c: *mut Checker, e: Expr) -> TypeEntry — convert check_call_expr (12475 target); same arg-traversal note.
checker_check_struct_lit_inplace(c: *mut Checker, e: Expr) -> TypeEntry — convert check_struct_lit (12484 target); field-init exprs via checker_check_opt_expr_inplace.

CROSS-CUTTING (all 9): NONE of these handlers may re-enter/exit expr depth. The by-value check_expr brackets the whole match with check_expr_depth (12431) / exit_expr_depth (12496), but the *mut dispatcher already owns depth accounting (2451-2455 enter, 2474-2476 exit). A converted handler must check the BODY of its source method ONLY, dropping the depth bracket, or depth double-counts.

specs.method:
Convert the by-value `ExprIdent` arm of `check_expr` (check.sio:12451-12468) to a *mut leaf function `checker_check_ident_expr_inplace(c: *mut Checker, e: Expr) -> TypeEntry`, then add an inline dispatch arm `ExprIdent => checker_check_ident_expr_inplace(c, e)` to `checker_check_expr_inplace` (the dispatcher at line 2450).

WHY THIS IS FULLY *mut-NATIVE AND NEEDS NO BRIDGE: the ExprIdent arm contains ZERO by-value Checker-returning calls. Its three operations are:
  (a) `(*c).env.lookup(e.name)` — returns a TypeEntry (already used verbatim across the *mut spine, e.g. check.sio:903, 1227, 1492).
  (b) `(*c).borrows.is_borrowed(e.name)` / `(*c).borrows.consume_linear(e.name)` — these are BorrowEnv methods returning `bool` / `(BorrowEnv, i64)` (small structs, NOT Checker). The store-back idiom `let r = (*c).borrows.consume_linear(name); (*c).borrows = r.0; ...r.1` is the EXACT established pattern already in the *mut spine at check.sio:2386-2387 (check_linear_consumed) and 2315/2321 (track). No multi-MB SRET buffer is allocated, so frame-isolation rule 3 is satisfied without any dedicated bridge.
  (c) `c2.report_error_at(...)` → `checker_report_error_at_inplace(c, ...)` (existing helper, check.sio:1980).
  (d) `c2.is_linear_type(ident_ty)` → `checker_is_linear_type_inplace(c, ident_ty)` (existing helper, check.sio:2067).
The by-value original used `var c2 = c` only because by-value semantics forced a fresh binding before mutating `borrows`/emitting errors; in the *mut world the mutations land directly on `(*c)`, so `c2` is dropped entirely. The original arm did NOT touch expr-depth (that is handled by the enclosing dispatcher), so the leaf does no depth bookkeeping. The return value is the bare `ident_ty` TypeEntry (was tuple slot `.1`).

Convert by-value `check_binary_expr(self, e) -> (Checker, TypeEntry)` (check.sio:12527, 7.2MB frame) into `checker_check_binary_expr_inplace(c: *mut Checker, e: Expr) -> TypeEntry`. Both operands are checked by recursing through the existing `checker_check_opt_expr_inplace` / `checker_check_expr_inplace` *mut spine (no by-value Checker copy). The two by-value child methods that only mutate via report-helpers — `check_binary_op_types` and `check_binary_units` — are converted to real *mut functions (`checker_check_binary_op_types_inplace`, `checker_check_binary_units_inplace`) because they never allocate a Checker SRET (op_types returns Checker only as `self`-threading, units returns `(Checker, TypeEntry)`; both are mechanical (*c) rewrites). The THREE remaining by-value Checker-RETURNING calls — `check_hyper_binary(c,...) -> (Checker, TypeEntry)`, `c.record_hyper_expr(...) -> Checker`, and the by-value-Checker parameter call `eval_const_int_opt_expr(c,...)` — are each placed in their OWN dedicated leaf bridge (`checker_check_hyper_binary_bridge`, `checker_record_hyper_expr_bridge`, `checker_eval_const_int_denom_bridge`) so their SRET / by-value-Checker buffers live in a leaf frame, never inline in the hot binary-expr function. Pure free functions that take no Checker and return no Checker (`binary_result_type`, `knowledge_binary_result`, `is_knowledge_type`, `knowledge_inner`, `is_error_or_unknown`, `ty_with_unit`, `has_effect_id`) are called inline unchanged. report_error_at/report_mismatch are replaced by existing `checker_report_error_at_inplace`/`checker_report_mismatch_inplace`. Dispatch is wired by adding an `ExprBinary => checker_check_binary_expr_inplace(c, e)` arm to `checker_check_expr_inplace`.

Convert by-value check_call_expr (check.sio:13229, -> (Checker, TypeEntry), 14.1MB SRET frame) into checker_check_call_expr_inplace(c: *mut Checker, e: Expr) -> TypeEntry. The hot path inlines ONLY the clean direct-function-call case (callee resolves to TyFn with fn_sig_id >= 0) using *mut state access via (*c). Every other case — the e.right=Some index-misdispatch guard, all ~25 call_expr_is_builtin_* prefixes, the contest-witness prefix, the multitest/hypothesis effect-mutation block, the array-like-callee indexing path, and the error/non-fn-callee fallback — is delegated WHOLESALE to the already-isolated by-value leaf bridge checker_check_expr_mut(c, e) (check.sio:1146). This is deliberate: those branches each call by-value (Checker,TypeEntry)-returning methods, and routing the whole Expr back through the single existing isolated bridge keeps zero by-value Checker SRET buffer in the hot frame. The three state-only by-value Checker-returning sub-calls in the TyFn path (check_call_args, check_callee_effects, release_call_arg_borrows) are each wrapped in their OWN new dedicated leaf bridge so the 12MB by-value-check_expr SRET they transitively allocate never lands in checker_check_call_expr_inplace's frame. Callee resolution reuses checker_check_opt_expr_inplace (already pure *mut/inplace, recurses through checker_check_expr_inplace).
deps: check_index_expr (check.sio:13042) — recurses via check_opt_expr->check_expr; currently absorbed by the checker_check_expr_mut bridge through the e.right guard, so NO standalone conversion required for this target, but it is the natural next inplace target

check_call_args / check_call_args_inner (check.sio:15340/15605) — recurses into check_expr per-arg; wrapped here by checker_check_call_args_bridge; a future true *mut conversion would let arg-checking run in place

check_expr_list_no_type_no_linear_consume / check_expr_list_no_type (check.sio:15680/15667) — recurses into check_expr; currently reached only via the checker_check_expr_mut fallback for error/non-fn callees, so no bridge added in this target

the ~25 call_expr builtin check_*_expr methods (check_prove_robust_expr, check_measure_expr, check_lift_knowledge_expr, check_contest_witness_expr, ...) — all return (Checker,TypeEntry) and recurse into check_expr; intentionally left on the checker_check_expr_mut by-value path
checker_check_opt_expr_inplace (check.sio:2435) — already pure *mut, REUSED for callee resolution; no work needed

specs.method:
Convert by-value `Checker::check_field_access` (check.sio:12911-13036, 9.6MB SRET frame) into a *mut leaf `checker_check_field_access_inplace(c: *mut Checker, e: Expr) -> TypeEntry`, then add an inline dispatch arm in `checker_check_expr_inplace` (line 2450) routing `ExprFieldAccess` to it instead of falling through to the 12.29MB by-value `checker_check_expr_mut`.

The conversion is fully *mut-clean and requires NO by-value bridge. The full call inventory of check_field_access shows exactly two Checker-by-value calls: `self.check_opt_expr(e.left)` and `c.report_error_at(...)`. Both already have *mut leaf replacements:
  - `self.check_opt_expr(e.left)` -> `checker_check_opt_expr_inplace(c, e.left)` (check.sio:2435; this itself recurses through checker_check_expr_inplace, keeping the receiver SRET out of THIS frame — the receiver's by-value path, if any, is isolated inside checker_check_expr_mut which is already a dedicated leaf).
  - `c = c.report_error_at(e.span, code, 0, 0, 0)` -> `checker_report_error_at_inplace(c, e.span, code, 0, 0, 0)` (check.sio:1980; returns unit, no reassignment).
Every other operation in the body returns a NON-Checker value and is a free function or a `(*c)` field read, all legal in *mut context: `(*c).structs.find/get`, `field_info_list_find`, `field_info_list_has`, `has_effect_id`, `knowledge_inner`, `name_matches_str{1,3,4,5,7}`, `type_entry_list_count`, `type_entry_list_get`, `is_error_or_unknown`, `ty_error/ty_f64`. (`(*c).structs.get(idx)` through-deref method call is attested at line 1237 `(*c).contests.get`; `(*c).structs.find` at line 2069.)

The single mechanical transform of the body: drop the `let pair = ...; var c = pair.0; let base_ty = pair.1` thread — replace with `let base_ty = checker_check_opt_expr_inplace(c, e.left)`; rewrite every `c = c.report_error_at(...)` to `checker_report_error_at_inplace(c, ...)`; and replace every `(c, <ty>)` tuple tail with a bare `<ty>` return (the function now returns the bare TypeEntry, no Checker). All `c.` field reads become `(*c).`.
deps: ExprIdent (currently _ => checker_check_expr_mut, 12.29MB by-value) — the dominant struct/tuple/Knowledge field-access RECEIVER; until inline-converted, `s.x` overflows on the receiver, not on this conversion
ExprStructLit (check_struct_lit) — receiver for inline `S{..}.field`
ExprCall (check_call_expr) — receiver for `f().field`
ExprPath (check_path_expr) — receiver for enum/qualified-path field bases

specs.method:
Convert by-value `check_method_call` (check.sio:13068, 15.0MB SRET frame) into `checker_check_method_call_inplace(c: *mut Checker, e: Expr) -> TypeEntry`. The body uses `(*c).field` access and never copies the Checker. The receiver is checked via the existing TypeEntry-returning `checker_check_opt_expr_inplace(c, e.left)`; errors via `checker_report_error_at_inplace(c, ...)`. The four remaining Checker-returning children (`check_expr_list_no_type_no_linear_consume`, `release_call_arg_borrows`, `check_call_args`, `check_callee_effects`) each return a bare `Checker` (no tuple), so they are wrapped in four NEW dedicated leaf bridges that store-back and return unit — never inlined into the hot function (frame-isolation rule). The dispatcher `checker_check_expr_inplace` gets a new `ExprMethodCall` arm so real programs stop hitting the 12.29MB by-value `checker_check_expr_mut` path.

KEY FRAME-ISOLATION NOTE: `check_expr_list_no_type_no_linear_consume(e.args)` occurs ~6× and `release_call_arg_borrows(...)` ~7× across the branches. EVERY occurrence must route through the single corresponding leaf bridge; not one may be inlined as `(*c).check_...()`, or the multi-MB SRET reappears in the hot frame.

`(*c).fn_sigs.find_method_semantic(base_ty, e.name)` (→i64) and `(*c).fn_sigs.get(sig_id)` (→FnSig) are read-only sub-object reads returning scalar/FnSig (not Checker), so they stay inline. `let call_start_borrows = (*c).borrows` is a BorrowEnv value copy captured BEFORE the expr_list bridge in each branch (the bridge mutates (*c).borrows), then passed into the release bridge.

Convert the COLLECT-side struct/enum prelude path to *mut, and—critically—extract the residual by-value `_ =>` arm of `checker_collect_item_inplace` into its own leaf bridge so the dispatcher stops carrying the 8-12MB by-value-Checker SRET frame.

DISCRIMINATOR justifying full-in-place (no by-value bridge for struct/enum): trace every transitive checker-touching callee.
- collect_struct_def → collect_field_defs → collect_field_def_list → lower_type_expr  (the ONLY checker-touching leaf) → already has *mut analog checker_lower_type_expr_mut.
- collect_enum_def → collect_variants → collect_variant_list → collect_field_defs → bottoms out in the same lower_type_expr.
Since every checker-touching call has a *mut analog, both paths convert FULLY in-place with NO by-value Checker ever materialized — exactly mirroring the existing checker_collect_fn_param_list_mut / MutParamListResult / checker_collect_fn_params_mut spine (check.sio:2135-2155).
